questions.answer: Coherent waves have a constant phase difference. This keeps maxima and minima at fixed positions so a stable pattern can be observed.
accepted_alternatives: Waves are coherent when their phase difference remains constant.

marking_points.text: States that coherence is a constant phase difference between two waves.
Explains that coherence keeps the interference pattern stable or keeps maxima and minima at fixed positions.

option_feedback.A: Correct. 7.5 cm is 1.5 wavelengths, an odd half-wavelength path difference.
option_feedback.B: A whole-number wavelength path difference would be constructive.
option_feedback.C: The question states that both waves arrive at P.
option_feedback.D: The in-phase sources have a fixed phase relationship.

marking_points.text: Selects A: complete destructive interference.

questions.answer: B. One signal generator feeding two loudspeakers of similar output.

option_feedback.A: Independent sources can drift in relative phase.
option_feedback.B: Correct. A common generator fixes the relative phase and similar outputs improve contrast.
option_feedback.C: A microphone detects; it is not a second wave source.

marking_points.text: Selects B: one signal generator feeding two loudspeakers of similar output.

questions.answer: A. Make the amplitudes more nearly equal.

option_feedback.A: Correct. More nearly equal amplitudes allow deeper cancellation at minima.
option_feedback.B: Phase drift moves and blurs the pattern.
option_feedback.C: Without overlap there is no interference pattern.

marking_points.text: Selects A: make the wave amplitudes at the observation region more nearly equal.

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Connect two loudspeakers to the same signal generator, aim them into a common overlap region, and move a microphone connected to a level meter through that region to record alternating maxima and minima.
accepted_alternatives: A sound-level sensor or oscilloscope may replace the level meter.

marking_points.text: Uses one signal generator to drive two loudspeakers.
Arranges the sound waves to overlap.
Moves a microphone or suitable detector through the overlap region to record alternating maxima and minima.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: Independent generators may not maintain a constant phase difference. The positions of constructive and destructive interference then move, so a detector does not record a stable pattern.

marking_points.text: States that independent generators may have a changing phase difference or are not coherent.
Explains that maxima and minima move or the observed pattern becomes unstable or blurred.

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Both slits are illuminated by the same incident wavefront from one monochromatic source, so the waves leaving them have the same frequency and a constant phase difference.

marking_points.text: States that both slits are illuminated by the same source or wavefront.
States that the emerging waves have the same frequency and a constant phase difference.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: The slits should be narrow enough for diffraction and close enough that the diffracted light overlaps on the screen. Other acceptable choices include comparable intensity from the slits and a screen or detector able to resolve the fringes.
accepted_alternatives: Any two valid, distinct conditions not already supplied in the stem; monochromatic light alone earns no credit because it is given.

marking_points.text: States one valid condition not supplied in the stem, such as narrow slits producing diffraction, sufficient overlap, close slit separation, comparable amplitudes or adequate resolution.
States a second distinct valid condition or design choice not supplied in the stem.

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: Alternating bright and dark fringes are observed.

marking_points.text: States that alternating bright and dark fringes are observed on the screen.

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Path difference = 1.44 - 1.26 = 0.18 m. In wavelengths, 0.18 / 0.12 = 1.5 wavelengths.
parts.unit_policy: Accept 0.18 m followed by 1.5 wavelengths; no physical unit on the final ratio.

marking_points.text: Calculates the path difference as 0.18 m.
Divides by 0.12 m and obtains 1.5 wavelengths.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: P is an intensity minimum because 1.5 wavelengths is an odd half-wavelength path difference, so waves from the in-phase sources arrive in antiphase and interfere destructively.

marking_points.text: Identifies 1.5 wavelengths as an odd half-wavelength path difference that gives antiphase arrival or destructive interference.
Concludes that P is at an intensity minimum.

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: Diffraction makes the microwaves spread after each opening. This creates a wider region where waves from both sources overlap, allowing maxima and minima to be detected across that region.

marking_points.text: States that diffraction makes the microwaves spread after the openings.
Explains that spreading creates a wider overlap region in which maxima and minima can be observed.
